title: Default-client redirect-budget acceptance test fails on keep-alive-dead pooled connections
claim: The dedicated acceptance test for the source-qualified default twenty-hop redirect budget fails deterministically on this audit host: the scripted redirect server closes each connection without advertising 'Connection: close', so the pooling default client (max_idle_per_host=10) reuses a dead keep-alive connection on a later 307 hop and the non-idempotent POST is not retried, surfacing Network('error sending request') instead of completing the chain. The explicit Limited(20) client passes the identical chain only because plain_client disables pooling. The test therefore conflates a test-harness keep-alive fidelity gap with the redirect-budget boundary and breaks the declared workspace gate at audit_head.

evidence.detail: failing test source_qualified_default_redirect_budget_has_exact_twenty_hop_boundary; panic '20 redirects must succeed; explicit=false'
redirect_response emits no 'Connection: close' header while Script::coalesced hard-closes the socket (serve_scripted lines 152-158)
plain_client sets max_idle_per_host(0), avoiding the dead-pool reuse that the default HttpClient (pool default 10) hits

evidence.location: audit execution log ( opi-ai suite, 2 runs + isolated rerun )
evidence.detail: 20 passed / 1 failed in-suite; isolated rerun with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 failed identically (deterministic)

criterion_source: docs/research/pi-ai-opi-ai-alignment/pi-1.3.0-rust-backends.md#RDF-22 (upstream HTTP acceptance profile; redirect budget twenty hops with typed refusal)

title: Mistral/OpenRouter compat fixture tests assert strict:true, contradicting the pinned source and the shipped implementation
claim: mistral_profile_inherits_shared_compat_flags and openrouter_profile_inherits_shared_compat_flags assert tools[0].function.strict == true for an unannotated tool on a strict_tool_schema profile. The pinned Pi 1.3.0 compat chat wire sends 'strict: strict ?? false' (false for unannotated tools), the opi-ai README documents 'unconstrained tools send strict: false on capable wires', and the shared adapter implements exactly that (default_strict: Some(false)). Both committed tests fail at audit_head, so the declared workspace gate cannot pass; the tests encode a misreading of strict_tool_schema as a per-tool default rather than a capability flag.

evidence.detail: assertion 'Mistral inherits strict-tool-schema from the shared compat path' expects strict == true; probe shows wire strict:false
same assertion for OpenRouter
pinned source: '...(compat.supportsStrictMode !== false && { strict: strict ?? false })'
chat_tool_options sets default_strict: Some(false); openai_responses_shared.rs:720 'strict = per_tool_strict.or(options.default_strict)'
documents 'unconstrained tools send strict: false on capable wires'

criterion_source: docs/research/pi-ai-opi-ai-alignment/pi-1.3.0-sdk-contracts.md#compat-schema (supportsStrictMode wire rules; strict projection per pinned source)

title: Session-affinity mapping test expects retention-gated suppression that neither the pinned source nor the implementation provides
claim: session_affinity_wire_mappings expects session-affinity headers (session_id / x-client-request-id / x-session-affinity) to be suppressed when cache_retention is Disabled. The pinned Pi 1.3.0 source emits those headers whenever a session id exists and sendSessionAffinityHeaders is set, and only the prompt-cache key is retention-gated (cacheSessionId = retention === 'none' ? undefined : sessionId); the registered compat rows likewise state affinity format is not equivalent to the cache key. The opi-ai implementation matches the source; the committed test contradicts it and fails at audit_head (observed: all three headers carried 'session-disabled').

evidence.detail: asserts header_value(chat_requests[3], name) == None; probe shows Some("session-disabled") for all three headers
affinity headers emitted on sessionId && sendSessionAffinityHeaders, independent of cache retention
cacheSessionId (prompt cache key) is the only retention-gated session use
affinity header emission unconditional on retention; prompt_cache_key gated by cache_retention != Disabled (lines 1869-1881)

title: Prepare-path credential failures reach consumers as StreamFailure(CredentialNeeded), defeating typed credential classification and login remediation
claim: When authentication resolution fails during prepared-call setup, models.rs wraps the raw CredentialNeeded cause with with_projection/with_partial into ProviderError::StreamFailure(CredentialNeeded) (response_received=false). opi-agent surfaces that wrapped shape to callers, and the product harness provider_auth_failure matches only the unwrapped ProviderError::CredentialNeeded, so interactive login remediation (interactive.rs), RPC auth mapping (rpc.rs) and runner auth exit codes miss prepare-time credential failures. opi-ai itself treats pre-handoff StreamFailure as preserving credential classification (EventStream bookkeeping unwraps it; ChatStream::into_stream_parts unwraps it), so the prepare-boundary wrap escapes that intent. The committed opi-agent acceptance test public_retry_retains_initial_steering_after_auth_preparation_failure fails at audit_head with exactly this shape.

evidence.detail: resolve_route_auth error mapped through models_error_cause(error).with_projection(&projection)
with_partial wraps any non-StreamFailure cause into StreamFailure{response_received:false}
EventStream classification unwraps pre-handoff StreamFailure to retain credential classification — the intent the prepare boundary violates
prepare/start_attempt errors become AgentError::Provider(AgentProviderFailure{error}) unchanged; AgentError::from never maps to AgentError::CredentialNeeded
provider_auth_failure matches only unwrapped ProviderError::CredentialNeeded/CredentialRevoked/AccountIdMissing
failing test; observed error AgentProviderFailure{error: StreamFailure(CredentialNeeded{provider_id:"mock"})}

criterion_source: docs/research/pi-ai-opi-ai-alignment/acceptance-matrix.md#V-05 (typed acquisition/auth failure classification preserved to callers)

title: Mistral Conversations adapter sends strict:true with converted schema for unannotated tools, diverging from the pinned Pi 1.3.0 wire
claim: MistralConversationsProvider::function_tool_value defaults unannotated tools to strict:true (unwrap_or(true)) and sends the strict-converted schema, while the pinned Pi 1.3.0 mistral-conversations toFunctionTools sends 'strict: strict ?? false' (false) with unconverted parameters for unannotated tools. The Rust doc comment misattributes the true default to Pi ('pi toFunctionTools: the strict projection defaults on'), the crate README documents the true default as opi behavior, and a committed test (tools_project_strict_default_true) locks the divergence in. No registered rust-differences record authorizes this wire deviation, so every unannotated tool on this adapter is enforced differently from the pinned source.

evidence.detail: function_tool_value: resolve_json_schema_strict_sampling(...).unwrap_or(true); parameters strict-converted; doc comment misattributes Pi
pinned source: 'const strict = resolveJsonSchemaStrictSampling(tool, true); ... strict: strict ?? false'
tools_project_strict_default_true asserts function.strict == true (locks divergence, passes)
documents 'Tools project strict: true by default with the converted schema' as opi behavior
no registered difference records a strict-default deviation for mistral-conversations

reproduction: cargo test -p opi-ai --test mistral_fixtures tools_project_strict_default_true -- --exact (locks the divergence)
